ety.text: Borrowed from Latin album (“blank white writing tablet”), from albus (“white”).

senses.d: In Ancient Rome, a white tablet or register on which the praetor's edicts and other public notices were recorded.
A book specially designed to keep photographs, stamps, or autographs.
ex: In his free time, he used to open his album and add new pictures to it.

senses.d: A collection, especially of literary items.
A phonograph record that is composed of several tracks.
A jacket or cover for such a phonograph record.
A group of audio recordings, on any medium, intended for distribution as a group.
ex: His albums are very popular on Spotify.
He has released 8 albums so far.

ety.text: From German Album, from Latin album (“blank white writing tablet”), from albus (“white”). Doublet of alvo.
Unadapted borrowing from German Album, from Latin album amīcōrum (literally “white thing of friends”). Doublet of albo. Cf. English album.

ety.text: Latin albumbor. Spanish álbum Borrowed from Latin album. Doublet of albo and obo.

From the Middle English expression al be it (that), itself shortened from althagh it be that (“although it be that”), and thus composed from al (“completely, entirely”, literally “all”) + be (3rd person singular present subjunctive of been (“to be”)) + it.

ex: Who are you? tell me for more certainty, / Albeit Ile ſweare that I do know your tongue.
There’s an easy, albeit expensive, way to fix the national crisis in forensic crime labs.
